summary: Qualitative verify of conflict-triage-fixture is complete. Spec intent is largely met (fail-open triage, output-only persist, three-hunk ClassRequired fixture, two-step CAS retry, pinned judges) and the two design questions stay open. Weighting edge cases and test quality: mechanical hunk resolutions are prompt-only, fixture packets cannot edit toy.go, and the rubric grades canned JSON rather than fixture evidence; tasks 2.1 and 3.4 do lock real git/gate behavior rather than restating it.

hard_stops.hard_stop: Executing mechanical test/build commands when mechanical results are already provided.
Any credential value would need to be chosen, generated, or written.
A done-criterion turns out to be impossible, or already true for a reason the packet did not anticipate.
Two reasonable interpretations exist for a spec requirement and the specification does not say which.
Satisfying one instruction in this packet would require violating another.

findings.finding: RunTriage does not enforce deterministic mechanical resolutions. pinBusinessHigh only overwrites business hunks to ARBITRARY and pins RiskBand high; slice_union / rename_vs_edit resolutions are whatever the invoker returned. The prompt asks for deterministic mechanical resolution, but Go never checks it. TestTriageAgent_BusinessHunkPinsHighRisk includes a slice_union hunk with Resolution union and never asserts that field after RunTriage; there is no rename_vs_edit coverage on the RunTriage path.

Fixture packet templates cannot produce the three-hunk ClassRequired toy. GenerateFixture conflicts on toy.go for both features; feat_a.md / feat_b.md grant only fixture/feat-a/ and fixture/feat-b/. Dispatching those packets cannot edit toy.go. Tests only parse the four packets and assert DisjointAllowedPaths success — they never dispatch, and they never prove the spec's overlapping combined-dispatch refusal.

EvaluateRubric grades canned TriagePayload JSON from stub binaries with an empty temp WorktreePath. It never presents GenerateFixture evidence to a judge. Isolation (model argv, no cross-provider strings) is a real executor.Run check and is the strongest rubric test. gradePayload requires three hunks, non-uniform kind/resolution, a business hunk flagged ARBITRARY, and two mechanical kinds — it does not require RiskBand high, and it does not score cause quality. Uniform rejection is locked. ProposedSHA is correctly ignored.

Invariant coverage through RunTriage is markers-only. Spec requires residual conflict markers or edits outside allowed paths to fail candidate validation. TestTriageAgent_InvariantViolationsFailCandidate writes leftover markers in toy.go and checks CandidateStatusFailed with Output retained — that locks the marker path and audit retention. Out-of-scope edits are locked on the helpers (task 2.1) but not through RunTriage. failOpenPayload omits ProposedSHA.

Missing/divergent base SHA skipping ClassRequired is proven at overlap.Evaluate, not through evaluateOverlapGate. fixture_test.go:113-119 calls Evaluate with an empty common base and expects ErrNoMergeBase. The gate's continue on that error is attempt.go:745-747 (pre-existing). There is no ExecuteAttempt test that a missing/divergent registered base_sha yields no awaiting request and no promotion block. Task 3.1 discloses this; the spec scenario is still the gate path.

validVerifyBudget is a weak format check: prefix ~ and substring ' min: '. Spec requires wall-clock duration plus a concrete command. '~4 min: ' with an empty command would pass; the business test only asserts the prefix/substring after an empty invoker budget is replaced with VerifyBudgetExample.

The business-hunk fixture property 'both sides compile and pass their own tests' is not locked. toy.go is a snippet (Price 100 vs 200, Tags literals, Helper vs HelperRenamed) with pad(25) so hunks stay farther apart than NearbyHunkLines=3. Tests assert Classify ClassRequired and hunk count 3; they never go-build or go-test the toy.

Apply-lane claim check: tasks 2.1 and 3.4 lock real terminal behavior, not tautologies. e949c95 added candidate_test.go without modifying candidate.go. TestScanConflictMarkers_DocumentationAndScriptPaths scans docs/README.md and script.sh as text, skips a NUL binary, and asserts the script was not exec'd (sentinel absent). TestEnforceAllowedPaths_ExplicitWorktreeCwd chdirs away and uses git -C. TestEnforceAllowedPaths_StagedAndUntrackedDisjoint asserts the 4-way union (committed/unstaged/staged/untracked) against base_sha. attempt_test.go GenerateFixture + ExecuteAttempt uses real overlap.Evaluate (EvaluateOverlap unset); matching-tip retry adopts the integrated SHA and PromoteCAS once; tip-drift commits on branch B and asserts no stale SHA and PromoteCAS count 0. TestReconcileResolve_RejectsLinkedWorktree creates a linked worktree, chdirs into it, and expects CLI refusal (cli.go:1478-1480).

findings.finding: The two design questions remain open. types.go states there is no numeric mapping; task 1.1 did not encode a formula; pinBusinessHigh is the spec ratchet (any business hunk → payload high), not thresholds for mixed composition. Rubric pins claude/claude-opus-5 and opencode/openai/gpt-5.6-sol only; RunTriage requires an injected TriageInvoker and names no production executor. No task closed either question.
